name.en: “Hi Mum, I’m stuck overseas”: family in trouble

how.en: Someone pretends to be a family member or friend, often travelling, and writes from a new number or WhatsApp account. They say they are in trouble (a lost phone, a missed flight, a bill to pay) and ask you to send money quickly. Scamwatch warns these messages rise in the holiday season.

text.en: A message arrives from an unknown number claiming to be your child or a friend.
They say they are overseas or travelling and in trouble.
They ask for money urgently, often to someone else’s account.
They avoid calls and push you to pay now.
Hi Mum, it’s me, I dropped my phone at the airport so this is my new number. My card isn’t working and I need to pay for the hotel tonight, can you transfer $950? I’ll pay you back when I’m home x

en: lost my phone at the airport

alguien finge ser mi hijo por whatsapp
me llego un mensaje de un numero desconocido
me piden dinero para una emergencia
me contactaron diciendo que estaban de viaje
pt: oi mae e meu numero novo
estou viajando e estou com problemas
alguem se passando pelo meu filho
recebi uma mensagem de um numero desconhecido
estao pedindo pix fingindo ser da familia
um parente disse que esta preso no exterior

en: A relative writes from a new number and asks for money.
An emergency while travelling that needs money now.
Paying into an account in someone else’s name.
They won’t talk on a call or video.
Call the person on the number you already have for them.
Ask a personal question a scammer couldn’t answer.
Don’t use the contact details in the message.

sources.title: Scam alert: Scammers don’t take holidays - but they can ruin yours
